docs.title: boti-dask
docs.text:
Dask sessions, resilient execution and cluster utilities for the Boti ecosystem.

import boti_dask costs about two milliseconds and imports no Dask; the first use of a Dask-backed name (DaskSession, safe_compute, …) imports distributed.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
uv add boti-dask                 # core: boti, dask[dataframe,distributed], pandas
uv add 'boti-dask[diagnostics]'  # numpy, polars, pyarrow for describe_frame on those engines
uv add 'boti-dask[k8s]'          # dask-kubernetes       -> cluster_kind="kubernetes"
uv add 'boti-dask[slurm]'        # dask-jobqueue         -> cluster_kind="slurm"
uv add 'boti-dask[coiled]'       # coiled                -> cluster_kind="coiled"
uv add 'boti-dask[otel]'         # OpenTelemetryProvider

docs.title: Three things it does
docs.text:
A verified session. dask_session opens a client against a scheduler address, a cluster backend or a local cluster, checks that the scheduler answers, that workers are present and that a task runs, and raises DaskSessionUnavailable within a deadline instead of hanging.

from boti_dask import dask_session, safe_compute
import dask

with dask_session(cluster_kwargs={"n_workers": 2, "processes": False}) as client:
    print(safe_compute(dask.delayed(lambda: 6 * 7)(), dask_client=client))

Resilient execution. safe_compute, safe_persist, safe_wait, safe_head and safe_gather (and their async_safe_* twins) retry once on a recoverable Dask error, re-resolve the client, and turn an orphaned graph into a readable RuntimeError.

Configuration from the environment. One prefix selects the scheduler or cluster kind, the connectivity check, the watchdog, telemetry and code uploads:

from boti_dask import dask_session_from_env_prefix

with dask_session_from_env_prefix("ETL_DASK_", env_file=".env") as client:
    ...

ETL_DASK_CLUSTER_KIND=slurm
ETL_DASK_CLUSTER_KWARGS={"queue": "batch", "cores": 8}
ETL_DASK_WATCHDOG_INTERVAL=30
ETL_DASK_TELEMETRY=otel
ETL_DASK_UPLOAD=./src/etl_jobs,rich>=13

docs.title: Changelog
docs.text: All notable changes to boti-dask are recorded here. The format follows Keep a Changelog; versions follow Semantic Versioning. Behaviour changes are in bold under Changed.

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
• {PREFIX}UPLOAD keeps extras and version ranges in one entry. The value was split on every comma, so pkg[a,b]>=1,<2 became four entries. Commas inside brackets or followed by a version operator (<, >, =, !, ~) no longer split; a value starting with [ is read as a JSON list of strings. ./src/etl_jobs,rich>=13 parses as before.
  • A directory upload is resolved before it is zipped. . or .. has no name of its own, so the archive held entries with a leading slash that no worker could import; the resolved directory's name is used instead, and the filesystem root is refused with a ValueError.
  • Derived shared keys, upload paths and settings kwargs stay out of logs and the scheduler dataset. The Reusing shared Dask session and Rebound Dask session lines log the session namespace (the explicit shared_key, or a digest of the derived key, which embeds repr(client_kwargs)) rather than the key text. Entries of the boti-dask:uploads dataset, readable by every client of the scheduler, are now kind:basename@digest rather than the local absolute path; the session log still names the full source. repr(DaskSessionSettings) shows the key names of cluster_kwargs and client_kwargs but not their values.
  • safe_* inspect the graph only when their logger is enabled for DEBUG. inspect_graph materialises the whole graph, and the wrappers ran it on every call (dry runs included) to log a line at INFO. They now skip it unless the logger would emit DEBUG, and log at that level; inspect_graph gains a level keyword (default "info") for direct use.
  • {PREFIX}CLUSTER_KWARGS accepts only sizing, placement and naming keys (ENV_CLUSTER_KWARGS). Dask cluster classes also take keys that load code at start-up (preload, worker_class, security, job-script prologues), and an environment file is not where that decision belongs. Other keys are refused with an error naming the accepted set; pass them as DaskSession(cluster_kwargs=...) in code.
  • An upload entry that names a missing path is an error. It was silently reclassified as a pip requirement and installed on every worker, so a mistyped path became a package install. Requirement strings must parse as PEP 508 (packaging.requirements.Requirement); option lines, ${VAR} expansion and direct-URL requirements are refused.
  • A shared session is rebound once, for every holder of its key. The pool entry now records its holders; a rebind points each of them at the new client, so the other holders' watchdogs probe the replacement instead of the client that was just closed and rebinding it in turn. The watchdog passes the client it probed as rebind(stale=...), which is a no-op when that client has already been replaced.
  • DaskSession.rebind() swaps only on success. The replacement is opened (and verified, when verification is on) before the old client is closed; a failed reconnect raises and leaves the session on its previous client, open and registered. The watchdog then keeps probing, doubling its interval after each failed rebind up to WatchdogConfig.max_backoff (default 300 s), rather than stopping. Watchdog.rebind_failures and Watchdog.delay expose the state; rebind_failed events carry next_probe_in.
  • safe_* no longer fall back to local compute in place of a cluster. A dask_client that was passed but is not running, with no running replacement discoverable, is a RuntimeError; so is losing the client mid-operation without a replacement to retry on (previously only DataFrame-like collections raised; delayed objects and futures were computed on the calling host). Calls that never named a client still run locally.
  • Cluster primitives refuse a client that is not running (RuntimeError) instead of quietly returning a process-local lock, semaphore or queue that gives no cluster-wide exclusion.
  • A semaphore re-requested with a different limit is a ValueError, on the cluster and in the process-local fallback alike; strict=False adopts the existing limit with a warning, as before.
  • cluster_semaphore, cluster_lock and cluster_queue take namespace, prefixed into the scheduler name (boti-dask:<namespace>:<name>), and DaskSession.namespace supplies one (the shared_key, else a digest unique to the session) so two sessions on one scheduler do not share a primitive by accident.
  • Symbolic links inside an uploaded directory are not shipped. A link in the tree used to send its target's bytes to every worker; links to files and directories are now skipped, and every file must resolve inside the resolved root.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• boti_dask.clusters: cluster_factory(kind), make_cluster(kind, **kwargs) and CLUSTER_KINDS select local, kubernetes (dask-kubernetes), slurm (dask-jobqueue) or coiled by name, importing the backend on first use. A missing backend raises ModuleNotFoundError naming the extra (k8s, slurm, coiled). DaskSessionSettings.cluster_kind / {PREFIX}CLUSTER_KIND maps to cluster_factory.
  • boti_dask.watchdog: WatchdogConfig and Watchdog probe the client on a daemon thread after open and call the new DaskSession.rebind() after failures_before_rebind consecutive failures. A managed session reopens; a shared session swaps the pool entry keeping its holders. Events reach the logger and an on_event callback; SessionPool.rebind_count() counts rebinds. DaskSession(watchdog=...), {PREFIX}WATCHDOG_INTERVAL, {PREFIX}WATCHDOG_FAILURES.
  • boti_dask.telemetry: TelemetryProvider protocol with NoopProvider (default), InMemoryProvider and OpenTelemetryProvider (otel extra). Spans around every safe_* and async_safe_* call; counters retries, rebinds, recoverable_errors; gauges workers, task_count, persisted_collections from DaskSession.record_gauges(). DaskSession(telemetry=...), configure_telemetry(), {PREFIX}TELEMETRY=none|memory|otel.
  • boti_dask.upload: DaskSession(upload=[...]) / {PREFIX}UPLOAD ships .py/.zip/.egg files, deterministically zipped directories, pure-Python wheels and pip requirement strings to the workers on open and after a rebind, skipping payloads whose SHA-256 the scheduler dataset boti-dask:uploads already holds. sync_uploads(client, items) does the same for any client.
  • boti_dask.STABLE and boti_dask.EXPERIMENTAL name each export's tier, and boti_dask.deprecated(name, removal, replacement=...) emits the DeprecationWarning used for transitions. The four modules above are experimental in 1.2.
  • A pytest-benchmark suite (benchmarks/, make bench) with a local baseline and a Benchmarks workflow; safe_compute adds about 2% to a bare client.compute locally.
  • A mkdocs-material site (docs/, uv run mkdocs serve) with an mkdocstrings reference, deployed per minor version by mike on release.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• The extra optional dependency is now diagnostics; boti-dask[extra] still resolves, as an alias of boti-dask[diagnostics].
  • DaskSession.__init__ accepts watchdog, telemetry and upload; existing arguments are unchanged.
  • SessionPool.debug_set_shared_ref_count is set_shared_ref_count.
  • The README is shorter; guides live in docs/guides/ and the reference in docs/reference/.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• cluster_semaphore, cluster_lock and cluster_queue: coordination primitives shared by name across the cluster when a running client exists (passed in, or discovered inside a worker task) and across the process otherwise, so dependents such as boti-data's partition fetch gate write one code path and never import distributed. Primitives obtained through a client are closed with it. A semaphore re-requested with a different limit keeps the first creator's limit and logs a warning.
  • ConnectivityCheck and DaskSessionUnavailable. DaskSessionSettings reads {PREFIX}CONNECTIVITY_TIMEOUT and {PREFIX}MIN_WORKERS.
  • A compatibility-matrix workflow that tests the floor, locked and latest versions of Dask and boti on every push, weekly, and on repository_dispatch type upstream-release.
  • This changelog.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• DaskSession verifies connectivity by default: a scheduler ping, a wait for min_workers (1) and one round-trip task, all within 10 s; a connect to a scheduler_address gets the same deadline unless client_kwargs sets timeout. Failure raises DaskSessionUnavailable naming the stage instead of hanging. Pass verify_connectivity=False to skip (for example around a stub client), or a ConnectivityCheck(timeout=..., min_workers=...) to tune it. DaskSessionSettings.verify_connectivity now defaults to True.
  • import boti_dask no longer imports Dask. Public names resolve lazily; DaskSessionSettings, describe_frame and inspect_graph work with no Dask on the path. Import time drops from about 510 ms to about 2 ms. Touching DaskSession or a safe_* wrapper imports distributed as before.
  • The standalone lockfile resolves against boti 1.2.0 (it pinned 1.0.5).
Last release before this changelog; see the git history.

docs.title: Stability
docs.text:
boti_dask.STABLE and boti_dask.EXPERIMENTAL name every exported symbol's tier.

  • Stable: the session (DaskSession, dask_session, DaskSessionSettings, connectivity), the safe_* and async_safe_* wrappers, diagnostics and the cluster primitives. Breaking changes to these arrive only with a major version, after at least one minor version in which the old form warns.
  • Experimental: clusters, watchdog, telemetry and upload, new in 1.2. Their signatures may change in a minor version; the changelog records every change in bold.

boti_dask.deprecated(name, removal) emits the DeprecationWarning boti-dask uses for the transition, naming the version in which the symbol goes away.

docs.title: Clusters API
docs.text:
boti_dask.clusters picks a cluster backend by name so deployment choice lives in configuration rather than in code.

Kind Cluster class Install extra local distributed.LocalCluster none kubernetes dask_kubernetes.operator.KubeCluster boti-dask[k8s] slurm dask_jobqueue.SLURMCluster boti-dask[slurm] coiled coiled.Cluster boti-dask[coiled]

docs.title: Symbols
docs.text:
• CLUSTER_KINDS: the tuple above.
  • cluster_factory(kind): the cluster class, imported on first use. A missing package raises ModuleNotFoundError naming the extra to install; an unknown kind raises ValueError.
  • make_cluster(kind, **cluster_kwargs): builds the cluster.

docs.title: From the environment
docs.text:
DaskSessionSettings.cluster_kind (env {PREFIX}CLUSTER_KIND) selects the backend; the existing {PREFIX}CLUSTER_KWARGS JSON is passed to it. A {PREFIX}SCHEDULER_ADDRESS takes precedence, since connecting to a scheduler builds no cluster.

Only sizing, placement and naming keys are accepted from the environment (boti_dask.session_settings.ENV_CLUSTER_KWARGS: n_workers, threads_per_worker, memory_limit, cores, memory, queue, walltime, name, namespace, image and the like). Keys that load code at start-up, such as preload, worker_class, security or a job-script prologue, are refused with an error: pass them as DaskSession(cluster_kwargs=...) in code, where they are reviewed with the rest of it.

export ETL_DASK_CLUSTER_KIND=slurm
export ETL_DASK_CLUSTER_KWARGS='{"queue": "batch", "cores": 8, "memory": "32GB"}'

from boti_dask import dask_session_from_env_prefix

with dask_session_from_env_prefix("ETL_DASK_") as client:
    ...

In code, DaskSession(cluster_factory=cluster_factory("kubernetes"), cluster_kwargs={...}) does the same. Each backend's own keyword arguments are documented by that project; boti-dask passes them through unchanged, except that local defaults dashboard_address to ":0".

docs.title: Diagnostics API
docs.text: boti_dask.diagnostics contains reusable diagnostics and metadata utilities.

docs.title: Primary symbols
docs.text:
• inspect_graph(...)
  • describe_frame(...)
  • diagnostics_logger(...)
  • UniqueValuesExtractor

docs.title: Typical usage
docs.text:
from boti_dask import inspect_graph, describe_frame, UniqueValuesExtractor

print(inspect_graph(ddf))
print(describe_frame(ddf))
values = await UniqueValuesExtractor().extract_unique_values(ddf, "id", limit=100)

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• inspect_graph materialises the whole graph, so its cost grows with the task count. It logs its metrics line at INFO when called directly (level="debug" lowers it). The safe_* wrappers only call it when their logger is enabled for DEBUG, and log at that level, so an INFO logger neither pays for the inspection nor sees the line (dry runs included).
  • describe_frame supports Dask, pandas, pyarrow, and polars objects.
  • UniqueValuesExtractor is best-effort and supports optional truncation via limit.

docs.title: Primitives API
docs.text: boti_dask.primitives gives dependents cluster-wide coordination without importing distributed themselves.

docs.title: Symbols
docs.text:
• cluster_semaphore(name, max_leases=1, *, client=None, namespace=None, strict=True)
  • cluster_lock(name, *, client=None, namespace=None)
  • cluster_queue(name, *, maxsize=0, client=None, namespace=None)

docs.title: Behaviour
docs.text:
• With a running client (passed in, or discovered through distributed.get_client(), which also works inside a task on a worker) the distributed primitive of that name is returned, shared by name across the whole cluster.
  • Without one, a threading.BoundedSemaphore, threading.Lock or queue.Queue of the same name is returned, shared by name across the process. Callers write one code path.
  • A client passed in must be running; a closed one raises RuntimeError rather than quietly handing back a process-local primitive that gives no cluster-wide exclusion.
  • A semaphore that already exists under the name with a different limit raises ValueError; strict=False adopts the existing limit and logs a warning.
  • Names are prefixed boti-dask: on the scheduler so they never collide with user primitives. Pass namespace=session.namespace (the shared_key, else a digest unique to the session) and the prefix becomes boti-dask:<namespace>: so two sessions on one scheduler stay apart.
  • Primitives obtained through a client are tracked by the session pool and closed when that client is closed by DaskSession.

docs.title: Typical usage
docs.text:
Bound the number of database connections a distributed load may open, cluster-wide:

from boti_dask import cluster_semaphore

def fetch_partition(spec):
    with cluster_semaphore("db:orders", max_leases=4):   # at most 4 across all workers
        return run_query(spec)

The same call made outside a cluster bounds the process instead, so local runs and tests need no special casing.

docs.text:
from boti_dask import safe_compute, safe_persist, safe_wait

persisted = safe_persist(ddf, dask_client=client)
safe_wait(persisted, dask_client=client, timeout=30)
result = safe_compute(persisted["id"].count(), dask_client=client)

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Handles recoverable communication errors with a single retry strategy.
  • Translates common orphaned graph failures into actionable runtime errors.

docs.title: Session API
docs.text: boti_dask.session provides explicit Dask client/session lifecycle helpers.

docs.title: Primary symbols
docs.text:
• DaskSession
  • DaskSessionSettings
  • dask_session(...)
  • dask_session_from_env_prefix(...)
  • recommended_dask_config(...)
  • apply_recommended_dask_config(...)
  • describe_client(...)
  • current_client_summary()
  • ConnectivityCheck
  • DaskSessionUnavailable
  • WatchdogConfig (see watchdog.md)

docs.title: Typical usage
docs.text:
from boti_dask import dask_session, describe_client

with dask_session(
    verify_connectivity=True,
    cluster_kwargs={"n_workers": 1, "threads_per_worker": 1, "processes": False, "dashboard_address": ":0"},
) as client:
    print(describe_client(client))

docs.title: Connectivity verification
docs.text:
verify_connectivity is on by default. Before DaskSession hands out a client it pings the scheduler, waits for min_workers (default 1) and runs one round-trip task, all within ConnectivityCheck.timeout (default 10 s). A connect to a scheduler_address is given the same deadline unless client_kwargs already sets timeout. Any failure raises DaskSessionUnavailable naming the stage that failed, instead of hanging on distributed's own timeouts.

from boti_dask import ConnectivityCheck, DaskSessionUnavailable, dask_session

try:
    with dask_session(
        scheduler_address="tcp://scheduler:8786",
        verify_connectivity=ConnectivityCheck(timeout=5, min_workers=2),
    ) as client:
        ...
except DaskSessionUnavailable as exc:
    ...  # fail fast; the cause is chained

Pass verify_connectivity=False to skip the check (for example around a stub client in tests). From the environment: {PREFIX}VERIFY_CONNECTIVITY, {PREFIX}CONNECTIVITY_TIMEOUT (seconds) and {PREFIX}MIN_WORKERS.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• shared=True + shared_key=... enables cross-context shared session reuse.
  • Session close emits a runtime warning when live persisted collections are tracked.
  • When dask_session(...) creates a local LocalCluster and dashboard_address is not set, it defaults to ":0" to avoid port 8787 contention.
  • DaskSessionSettings.from_env_prefix(...) supports typed env-backed loading for scheduler_address, shared, shared_key, verify_connectivity, connectivity_timeout, min_workers, cluster_kwargs (JSON), client_kwargs (JSON), cluster_kind, watchdog_interval and watchdog_failures.
  • DaskSession.rebind() replaces a dead client with a fresh connection; the watchdog calls it.

docs.title: Telemetry API
docs.text:
boti_dask.telemetry reports what the resilient wrappers and sessions do, through a provider of your choosing. The default provider records nothing and costs one attribute lookup per call.

Provider What it does Needs NoopProvider Nothing (default). InMemoryProvider Keeps spans, counters and gauges in lists and dicts. OpenTelemetryProvider Spans via opentelemetry.trace, instruments via opentelemetry.metrics, using the tracer and meter providers the application configured. boti-dask[otel]

docs.title: What is recorded
docs.text:
• Spans: one per safe_compute, safe_persist, safe_wait, safe_head (through its inner safe_compute) and safe_gather call, named after the wrapper with a remote attribute. The async_safe_* wrappers open an outer span in the caller's context around the thread offload.
  • Counters: recoverable_errors (a RECOVERABLE_DASK_ERRORS exception caught), retries (a retry against a live client attempted) and rebinds (DaskSession.rebind(), explicit or by the watchdog).
  • Gauges: workers, task_count (tasks executing across workers) and persisted_collections (tracked by the session pool), published by DaskSession.record_gauges() on open and after a rebind, and callable at any time.

OpenTelemetry instrument names are prefixed boti_dask..

docs.title: Selecting a provider
docs.text:
from boti_dask import OpenTelemetryProvider, configure_telemetry, dask_session

configure_telemetry(OpenTelemetryProvider())        # process-wide
# or per session, which installs it on open:
with dask_session(telemetry=OpenTelemetryProvider()) as client:
    ...

From the environment: {PREFIX}TELEMETRY=none|memory|otel.

Any object with span(name, **attributes) returning a context manager, add(counter, value=1, **attributes) and gauge(name, value, **attributes) satisfies TelemetryProvider.

docs.title: Upload API
docs.text:
boti_dask.upload ships code to the workers once per scheduler. Give DaskSession (or dask_session) an upload list and every payload is sent on open and again after a rebind; payloads the scheduler has already seen are skipped.

from boti_dask import dask_session

with dask_session(
    scheduler_address="tcp://scheduler:8786",
    upload=["./src/etl_jobs", "./dist/etl_jobs-1.4.0-py3-none-any.whl", "rich>=13"],
) as client:
    ...

From the environment: {PREFIX}UPLOAD as a comma-separated list (./src/etl_jobs,rich>=13) or a JSON list of strings (["pkg[a,b]>=1,<2", "./src/etl_jobs"]). In the comma-separated form a comma inside brackets or before a version operator stays inside its entry, so pkg[a,b]>=1,<2 is one requirement, not four.

A path entry must exist; a missing one is an error rather than a package name, so a mistyped path never becomes a pip install on every worker. Requirement entries must be plain PEP 508 strings (rich>=13, pkg[extra]; python_version >= "3.11"): option lines, ${VAR} expansion and direct-URL requirements are refused.

Payload How it ships .py, .zip, .egg, .pyz file Client.upload_file; workers import or add it to sys.path. Directory Zipped deterministically (sorted entries, fixed timestamps, caches skipped) as <name>.zip, then upload_file. The resolved directory name becomes the importable package, so . ships under the current directory's name; the filesystem root is refused. Pure-Python .whl Copied under a .zip name so workers add it to sys.path. Wheels with compiled extensions need a requirement string instead. Anything else (a requirement string) One PipInstall worker plugin per sync; pip runs on each worker.

docs.title: Deduplication
docs.text:
Each payload gets a SHA-256 digest (of the file bytes, the deterministic zip, or the requirement text). Digests of everything sent are stored in the scheduler dataset boti-dask:uploads, so a second session against the same scheduler only sends what changed. A fresh cluster has no dataset and receives everything. Every client of the scheduler can read the dataset, so each entry records only the payload kind, its base name and a short digest (directory:etl_jobs@3f1a…), never a local directory; the session log still names the full source.

sync_uploads(client, items, logger=None) does the same for an existing client and returns the payloads it sent.

docs.title: Watchdog API
docs.text:
boti_dask.watchdog keeps a DaskSession honest after it has opened. A Watchdog runs the same probe the session runs on open (scheduler ping, min_workers wait, one round-trip task) every interval seconds on a daemon thread. After failures_before_rebind consecutive failures it calls DaskSession.rebind(), which replaces the dead client with a fresh connection to the same scheduler address or cluster factory.

from boti_dask import ConnectivityCheck, WatchdogConfig, dask_session

def on_event(event: dict) -> None:
    print(event["event"], event)   # probe_failed / rebinding / rebound / rebind_failed / recovered

with dask_session(
    scheduler_address="tcp://scheduler:8786",
    watchdog=WatchdogConfig(interval=30, failures_before_rebind=3,
                            check=ConnectivityCheck(timeout=5), on_event=on_event),
) as client:
    ...

From the environment: {PREFIX}WATCHDOG_INTERVAL (seconds, enables the watchdog) and {PREFIX}WATCHDOG_FAILURES (default 3).

docs.title: What rebind does
docs.text:
• The replacement is opened (and verified, when verification is on) before the old client is closed. A failed reconnect raises and leaves the session on its previous client; the watchdog keeps probing, doubling its interval after each failed rebind up to max_backoff.
  • Managed session: opens a new client (and cluster), then closes the old ones. Live persisted collections on the old client are lost, exactly as on close, and the same warning is raised.
  • Shared session: swaps the pool entry under the per-key creation lock, keeps the holder count and points every holder of the key at the new client, so one rebind serves them all. rebind(stale=client) does nothing when client has already been replaced; the watchdog uses it so two holders never rebind the same outage twice.
  • External client: cannot be rebound; rebind() raises RuntimeError.

SessionPool.rebind_count() counts rebinds across the process; the telemetry provider exports it as the rebinds counter.

docs.title: Events
docs.text:
The Rebound Dask session key=... line names a shared session by its namespace: the explicit shared_key, or a digest of the derived pool key (which embeds the cluster and client keyword arguments and is never logged in full); None for a managed session.

Every transition goes to the session logger and to on_event as a dict with event and shared_key plus event-specific fields (failures, error, rebinds). Exceptions raised by on_event are swallowed and logged at debug level; they never stop the watchdog.

docs.title: boti_dask.clusters
docs.text:
Cluster backends selected by name: local, kubernetes, slurm and coiled.

Each backend is a third-party cluster class imported only when asked for, so this module costs nothing until :func:cluster_factory runs. A missing backend package raises a :class:ModuleNotFoundError that names the boti-dask extra to install, in the spirit of boti-data's dataframes_required.

docs.title: normalise_cluster_kind(kind)
docs.text: Lower-case and validate kind, raising ValueError listing the known kinds.

docs.title: cluster_factory(kind)
docs.text: Return the cluster class for kind, importing its package on first use.

docs.title: make_cluster(kind, **cluster_kwargs)
docs.text:
Instantiate a cluster of kind with cluster_kwargs.

docs.title: boti_dask.primitives
docs.text:
Cluster-wide coordination primitives with process-local fallbacks.

cluster_semaphore, cluster_lock and cluster_queue return the distributed primitive of the same name when a running client is available (passed in, or discovered with distributed.get_client() -- which also works inside a task on a worker), and a threading / queue equivalent of the same name otherwise. Either way the object is shared by name: two callers asking for cluster_lock("etl") get the same lock, cluster-wide or process-wide. Callers write one code path and never import distributed.

A client passed in explicitly must be running; a closed one is an error, not a quiet fall back to the process. namespace (for example DaskSession.namespace) is prefixed into the name so two sessions on one scheduler never share a primitive by accident.

Cluster primitives obtained through a client are tracked on the session pool and closed when that client is closed.

docs.title: cluster_semaphore(name, max_leases=1, *, client=None, namespace=None, strict=True)
docs.text:
A semaphore shared by name across the cluster, or across this process.

Returns distributed.Semaphore (acquire/release/context manager, acquire(timeout=...)) or threading.BoundedSemaphore. A semaphore that already exists under name with a different limit is a ValueError; with strict=False the existing limit is adopted and a warning logged.

docs.title: cluster_lock(name, *, client=None, namespace=None)
docs.text: A lock shared by name across the cluster, or across this process.

docs.title: cluster_queue(name, *, maxsize=0, client=None, namespace=None)
docs.text:
A FIFO queue shared by name across the cluster, or across this process.

Both forms expose put(item, timeout=...) and get(timeout=...).

docs.text:
Per-key lock held by DaskSession.open() across acquire-or-create.

Without it, two concurrent first opens of the same key both miss try_acquire_shared_session and both create a cluster; the second register_shared_session then overwrites the first entry, leaking the first cluster and corrupting the ref count.

docs.title: DaskSession
docs.text:
Bases: SessionRebindMixin, ManagedResource

A Dask distributed session backed by a :class:ManagedResource lifecycle.

Accepts an existing client, connects to a scheduler address, or creates a cluster. Supports shared (multi-holder) and managed (single-holder) sessions.

verify_connectivity (default on) pings the scheduler, waits for a worker and runs one task within :class:ConnectivityCheck.timeout; failure raises :class:DaskSessionUnavailable. telemetry becomes the process provider on open (:mod:boti_dask.telemetry). upload ships code to the workers on open and after a rebind (:mod:boti_dask.upload). watchdog keeps probing after open and calls :meth:rebind after repeated failures (:mod:boti_dask.watchdog); it applies to clients the session creates.

docs.title: namespace property
docs.text:
Prefix for this session's cluster primitives (:mod:boti_dask.primitives).

The explicit shared_key when given; otherwise a digest of the derived pool key for a shared session, or of this object's identity for a managed one, so two sessions never share a primitive by accident.

docs.title: boti_dask.telemetry
docs.text:
Telemetry hooks: spans around the safe_* wrappers and session counters/gauges.

A :class:TelemetryProvider is anything with span, add and gauge. Three are provided: :class:NoopProvider (the default, costs one attribute lookup), :class:InMemoryProvider (records everything, for tests and diagnostics) and :class:OpenTelemetryProvider (behind the otel extra). One provider is active per process (:func:configure_telemetry); a :class:~boti_dask.DaskSession built with telemetry= installs it on open.

Counters: retries, rebinds, recoverable_errors. Gauges: workers, persisted_collections, task_count.

docs.title: TelemetryProvider
docs.text: Bases: Protocol

docs.title: NoopProvider
docs.text: Records nothing; the default.

docs.title: InMemoryProvider dataclass
docs.text: Keeps spans, counters and gauges in memory; thread-safe.

docs.title: OpenTelemetryProvider
docs.text:
Spans through opentelemetry.trace and instruments through opentelemetry.metrics.

Uses whatever tracer and meter providers the application configured globally; boti-dask never installs exporters itself. Needs the otel extra (opentelemetry-api and opentelemetry-sdk).

docs.title: boti_dask.upload
docs.text:
Ship code to the workers once: files, directories, pure-Python wheels and requirements.

:func:sync_uploads sends each payload through Client.upload_file (files, directories zipped deterministically, wheels renamed so workers put them on sys.path) or a PipInstall plugin (requirement strings), and records the SHA-256 of every payload in the scheduler dataset boti-dask:uploads so a later session against the same scheduler skips what is already there.

docs.text: Bases: StrEnum

docs.title: Payload dataclass
docs.text: One thing to ship and the digest that identifies it on the scheduler.

docs.title: label property
docs.text:
What the scheduler dataset records: kind, base name and a short digest.

The dataset is readable by every client of the scheduler, so a path payload is labelled by its base name alone, never its directory.

docs.title: description property
docs.text: Kind and full source, for the local log only.

docs.title: classify_payload(item)
docs.text:
Decide how item ships and compute its digest; the digest never touches the cluster.

A path must exist: a missing one is an error rather than a package name, so a mistyped path never turns into a pip install on every worker.

docs.title: sync_uploads(client, items, *, logger=None)
docs.text: Send every payload in items the scheduler has not seen; return those sent.

docs.title: boti_dask.watchdog
docs.text:
Background health checks that rebind a :class:DaskSession after repeated failures.

A :class:Watchdog runs the same probe :class:DaskSession uses on open (a scheduler ping, a wait for min_workers and one round-trip task) every interval seconds on a daemon thread. After failures_before_rebind consecutive failures it asks the session to :meth:~DaskSession.rebind, which replaces the dead client with a fresh connection to the same target. A rebind that fails leaves the session on its previous client; the watchdog keeps probing, doubling its interval after each failed rebind up to max_backoff. Each transition is reported through on_event and the session logger, so an application can alert, back off or shut down on its own terms.

docs.title: WatchdogConfig dataclass
docs.text:
How often to probe, how many misses to tolerate, how far to back off, and whom to tell.

max_backoff caps the probe interval while rebinds keep failing: the interval doubles after each failed rebind and returns to interval once a rebind succeeds or a probe passes.

docs.title: Watchdog
docs.text: Probe a session's client on a timer and rebind it after repeated failures.

docs.title: delay property
docs.text: Seconds until the next probe: interval doubled per failed rebind, capped.

docs.title: tick()
docs.text: One probe; public so tests and schedulers can drive it without the thread.
